$schema_note: Physical and process safety thresholds for the CEA/aquascaping program. Every value is sourced to a specific document/section from knowledge/cea/. Values not present in any source document are marked "source": "TBD — needs domain expert input" rather than invented. Agents (especially security-safety-reviewer and the botany/electronics/mechanical specialists) MUST treat this file as the ground truth for physical safety gates and MUST stop and ask a human rather than guess when a threshold they need is not here.

ppfd_operating_band_umol_m2_s.source: Phase A §1.1, §2.3, §2.4; corroborated by Rack A Specification §00 (PPFD band 150-210 pmol-m2-s) and Rack A Manufacturing Pack QC criterion for T2 (PPFD 150-210, CV < 15%)

photoperiod_microgreens_hours.note: 24h continuous increases yield/phytochemicals but raises energy draw; tradeoff, not a hard rule

lighting.photoperiod_saffron_induction: low-to-moderate light during cool induction phase; no numeric photoperiod given

dli_mol_m2_day.note: Not stated directly as DLI in any source document. It is derivable from PPFD x photoperiod (e.g. 210 umol/m2/s x 18h -> ~13.6 mol/m2/day) but that derived figure is NOT itself sourced text, so it is not recorded here as a rule. Compute per-crop from the PPFD and photoperiod values above if a DLI figure is needed, and flag the computed value as derived, not sourced.

vpd_kpa.control_note: Computed from T and RH by the controller — never sensed directly

canopy_air_velocity_m_s.source: Phase A §1.4; Rack A Specification §05; Rack A Manufacturing Pack §01; CEA_Room_-_Floor_Plan.ocr.md §06

canopy_velocity_coefficient_of_variation.note: Two slightly different action thresholds appear in the source set for when the CV is bad enough to require the Phase-2 ducted plenum retrofit. Flagging both rather than picking one.

floor_plan_commissioning_threshold_pct.action: below 20%: plenum is an optimisation only; above 20%: plenum is a required fix

co2_safety_alarm_ppm.source: CEA_Room_-_Floor_Plan.ocr.md §06 ("CO2 safety: Alarm at 5000 ppm, fail-closed solenoid")

climate.co2_asphyxiation_context: A 22 kg CO2 cylinder released into a 60.2 m3 room produces roughly 12 m3 of gas (~20% of room volume) — lethal well before it is noticed. This is why the CO2 cylinder is sited on the terrace with only the regulated line entering the room, and why the low-level fail-closed monitor is non-optional. Source: CEA_Room_-_Floor_Plan.ocr.md §06.

electrical_load_phase_imbalance_target_p.note: As-designed 11-rack layout actually lands at ~20% imbalance on single-phase HVAC; resolved by specifying 3-phase HVAC. Documented as an open engineering finding, not a clean pass.

ph_operating_target.note: Operating/growing target for the nutrient solution.

ph_recovery_water_accept_gate.note: Wider pass/fail gate (G2) applied to recovered/reused water before it is allowed back into the rising main — distinct from the tighter 5.6-6.2 growing target above. OCR on this page ("45-75") is a high-confidence read of "4.5-7.5" given the pH context, but treat as needing a quick sanity check against the source PDF if this value drives a code path.

ec_operating_target.note: Phase A identifies EC as a dominant control variable (n=36 studies) but states no numeric target range. Phase D specifies sensor measurement range (0-5,000+ uS/cm) but that is instrument spec, not a target/safety threshold.

ec_recovery_water_accept_gate.note: Gate G1 in Closed-Loop_Water_Recovery.ocr.md §07 exists ("EC < setpoint x ~1.2, action: trough dump valve to waste on failure") but the OCR of the exact numeric threshold on this page ("< 15 setpoint — < 180 mS/cm at a 1.20 setpoint") is garbled/inconsistent (180 mS/cm is implausibly high for nutrient solution EC) and should NOT be trusted for an implementation. Needs a plain-Claude visual pass on Closed-Loop Water Recovery.pdf page 8 before this gate is coded.
ec_recovery_water_accept_gate.source: Closed-Loop_Water_Recovery.ocr.md §07 gate G1 — OCR UNRELIABLE, needs visual review

solution_temperature_c.action: MV-01 (terrace master supply valve) inhibited if solution temperature exceeds 28C; gate G3 holds 60 min and re-tests before dumping recovered water above 26C
solution_temperature_c.note: Above 26C, dissolved O2 drops (9.1 mg/L at 20C -> 7.6 mg/L at 30C -> 6.4 mg/L at 40C) and Pythium zoospore activity rises sharply in that band.

uv_disinfection_dose_mj_cm2.note: 100 mJ/cm2 is stated as the horticultural design dose for oomycete/bacterial control (Pythium, Fusarium). Gate G5 requires UV intensity >=70% of rated and lamp on before a recovery batch may transfer.

flood_and_drain_timing.standpipe_minimum_bore: DN32 (DN25 rejected — passes exactly the fill rate at 8mm head over the crest, i.e. zero margin; DN32 passes 11.9 L/min, a 1.65x margin)
flood_and_drain_timing.note: Leak/blocked-drain interlock: fill solenoids must be proven to close within 60 seconds during commissioning with a deliberately blocked drain. This is a QC HOLD POINT, not a design assumption.
flood_and_drain_timing.source: Rack A Specification §01, §05, §11; Rack A Manufacturing Pack §02 (check 7, T-tests), §12 QC checklist

pump_duty_cycle.rationale: Sequential (one tier at a time) filling costs ~11 minutes of cycle time — irrelevant at 1-3 cycles/day — but caps pump duty and pipe size so the pump/main never has to grow with rack count (20 racks need the same 7.2 L/min pump as 1). Note: this rule is superseded on the SUPPLY side once the terrace gravity-feed design (Rev 3) is adopted — gravity has spare head to flood all 4 tiers of a rack at once (Closed-Loop_Water_Recovery.ocr.md §02). Sequential DRAINING remains mandatory in all revisions because the recovery trough/gate logic is sized for one rack's batch (46L) against a 79L trough.

recovery_batch_run_limit_min.action: P-02 stops on low-level switch OR a 4-minute run limit, whichever first — the run limit specifically catches a stuck float

blowdown_pct_of_returned_volume.schedule: daily at 02:00, first batch of the day dumped regardless of gate result — this is deliberate salt control, not an error condition

alternative_day_night_regime_c.note: Reported as optimal for corm development in a separate greenhouse study

high_temp_stress_reference_c.note: 10C above optimum; used as a stress-research reference point, not an operating setpoint

electrical_fail_safes.rcbo_rationale: LED drivers and PWM/EC fans (and inverter-compressor HVAC) produce pulsating DC residual currents that a Type AC RCD/RCBO can fail to trip on. This is repeated as a hard requirement across every electrical section of the source set.

rcbo_ratings.terrace_circuit: 10 mA RCBO (tighter than room circuits, because it's an outdoor/wet installation)

electrical_fail_safes.surge_protection: Type 1+2 SPD at the main distribution board; Type 2 SPD per group panel (one per 8 racks), 10 kA, max 3m lead to earth bar
electrical_fail_safes.earthing: TN-S per IS 3043; every rack frame bonded, continuity < 0.1 ohm, tested and recorded per rack
electrical_fail_safes.elv_boundary: All conductors at or below bed/canopy level are 24V or 48V DC only. Mains (230V) is confined to an IP65 enclosure mounted above canopy height. This ELV boundary — not ingress rating — is what the source material calls the thing that makes the electrical and water systems genuinely independent.
electrical_fail_safes.emergency_stop: Room-level E-stop only (one latching mushroom head per aisle/door), NOT per-rack. Drops the group contactor / all fill solenoids / MV-01 / all pumps. Rationale given: 16 rack-level E-stops is 16 devices nobody can reach in an emergency; the per-rack isolator is for lock-out/tag-out maintenance, a different function.
electrical_fail_safes.source: Rack A Specification §07; Rack A Manufacturing Pack §01, §05; CEA_Room_-_Floor_Plan.ocr.md §05; Closed-Loop_Water_Recovery.ocr.md §08; Phase A §2.6

valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.note: De-energized (power-loss) state for every controlled wet-side device in the current design. This table is safety-critical and should be treated as authoritative for any firmware/controller work touching these devices.
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.rack_drain_solenoids: OPEN — beds self-drain; no standing water left on a dead/powerless rack
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.terrace_master_supply_valve_MV-01: CLOSED (spring-return) — the only thing holding back a full terrace reservoir must not be electricity
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.diverter_valve_FV-01: TO WASTE — unverified/unreused water can never enter the rising main without power and a passed gate
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.trough_dump_valve: CLOSED — a power cut must not silently discard a good, gate-passed batch
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.make_up_float_valve: MECHANICAL float valve (not solenoid) — keeps working through a power cut by design, not by control logic
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.vacuum_breaker: Passive device at the down-main high point — prevents a downstream failure from siphoning the terrace tank
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.overflow_design_rule: Every vessel keeps a gravity overflow one nominal size larger than its largest inlet, terminating with a visible air gap. An overflow that discharges into a closed pipe is explicitly called out as NOT an overflow — it becomes a second way to pressurise the tank.
valve_and_actuator_fail_safe_states.source: Closed-Loop_Water_Recovery.ocr.md §08; Rack A Specification §01, §11; Rack A Manufacturing Pack §01

tip_over_unanchored_rack.note: Height:depth ratio 3.48:1 is below the 4:1 threshold at which anchoring is normally mandated, so freestanding is technically defensible — but the empty-rack case (139N, ~14kgf) is called out as "genuinely marginal" and wall anchors are specified as mandatory, not optional, in the actual BOM/assembly instructions.
tip_over_unanchored_rack.source: Rack A Manufacturing Pack §02 check 6, §11 assembly step 08

terrace_slab_loading_kn_m2.note: Explicitly flagged in the source as needing a structural engineer's sign-off against the building's actual drawings before the terrace tank is ordered — the one item in the Water Recovery doc the authors say cannot be resolved by choosing better equipment.

open_structural_items_not_yet_closed.item: Depth-plane bracing (relying on decks as horizontal diaphragms instead of per-tier cross beams) has not been verified by frame analysis; tip-over numbers assume it holds.
open_structural_items_not_yet_closed.closes_by: Prototype sway test T16 (300N horizontal, front-back and side, residual deflection < 5mm)
open_structural_items_not_yet_closed.source: Rack A Specification §10; Rack A Manufacturing Pack §02, §13

open_structural_items_not_yet_closed.item: Canopy velocity uniformity for the Phase-1 (no ducted plenum) rack build is unmeasured; point-source fan is expected to produce ~33% CV vs ~10% for the Phase-2 ducted plenum.
open_structural_items_not_yet_closed.closes_by: 5-point-per-tier hot-wire anemometer traverse at commissioning and quarterly
open_structural_items_not_yet_closed.source: Rack A Specification §01, §05; Rack A Manufacturing Pack §09; CEA_Room_-_Floor_Plan.ocr.md §04
